sources.entry: CryptPad - Collaboration suite built to enable collaboration, synchronizing changes to documents in real time. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Nodejs/Docker
CryptPad | Collaboration suite that is end-to-end encrypted

summary.one_liner: CryptPad is an open-source, end-to-end encrypted collaboration suite that synchronizes document edits in real time.
summary.what_it_does: CryptPad is a collaboration suite that synchronizes changes to documents in real time. Data is encrypted in the user's browser before it is sent to the server, so the stored content is unreadable to someone who breaches the database. Account access is based on cryptographic keys derived from the username and password, so the server never sees either. The README says a correctly configured instance includes safeguards against collaborators injecting scripts into documents or uploads. Production deployment requires extra configuration described in a separate admin guide, and the README points to a development guide for a local instance without HTTPS. Official Docker images for AMD64 and ARM64 are published on Docker Hub, with Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml and docker-entrypoint.sh at the repository root.
use_cases: sharing documents with privacy from the server operator
running an end-to-end encrypted office suite via Docker
private collaboration where the host cannot read content
how_to_run: For a local development instance, follow the developer guide referenced in the README (no HTTPS or advanced security features).
For production, follow the admin installation guide referenced in the README.
Docker: use the Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml and docker-entrypoint.sh at the repository root, or pull the official image from Docker Hub.
notable: End-to-end encryption performed in the browser; keys derived from username and password so the server never sees credentials
Official Docker images for AMD64 and ARM64, published on Docker Hub since v5.4.0 (July 2023)
Translations handled through a Weblate instance, usable from a web browser alone
Developed by XWiki SAS; funded by French state research grant and NLnet, NGI TRUST, NGI DAPSI and other sources
caveats: The encryption code is served from the host like any web page, so users must trust the administrator to deliver untampered code
Operators can still see IP addresses and activity unless users access the instance through Tor Browser
Production setup requires additional configuration beyond the development instance
keywords: collaborate on documents without server access
